items.title: [BugFix][WeightTransfer] Fix DeepSeek-V4 Flash Vision reload with native retention
items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes the one-card DeepSeek-V4 Flash Vision sleep → wake → NPU IPC reload path and adds an end-to-end vision weight-transfer lane. This follows #18630 and #19248 and uses the existing Worker `sleep_preserve_parameter_names` mechanism from #18838. The source branch starts from the official upstream main base recorded at the end of **Regression scope**; the contributor fork only hosts the source branch. The production changes are implemented on that base rather than inheriting the production commits from #19248.

#### The fixes

1. **Reuse native multimodal processing.** Remove the obsolete four-argument `_call_hf_processor` override and its tokenizer thread cache. The pinned vLLM processor handles normalized image inputs and text processing through its existing interface.
2. **Let Worker restore weightless normalization state.** Register the existing `RMSNorm(has_weight=False).weight` tensor as a nonpersistent buffer, preserving its object and attribute name. Native buffer backup/restoration and `Module.to()` can then manage it. Traverse `modules()` because quantization modules can overload `apply()`.
3. **Derive vision markers from current parameters.** Build the sentinel table from the current `image_start`, `image_pad`, `image_newline` and `image_end` values on each forward, with the requested dtype/device, instead of retaining a detached stale table across weight updates.
4. **Fill omitted preserved parameters through native reload.** At update start, record the current parameters selected by the existing retention configuration, once per actual owning module. At finish, consult native layerwise loading records and submit only parameters omitted by the trainer to their original reload loaders. Trainer-supplied new values take precedence. This avoids duplicate accounting through shared module paths and prevents early completion from suppressing later incoming values. Transaction references are cleared in `finally`.

Implementation changes are limited to four production files and six test files. The production diff is +56/-74 lines. The existing Worker, RoPE, HCCL, packed transport and global reload skip sets remain at the historical base; no new production environment variable is introduced. The E2E helper adds checkpoint-compatible vision/aligner/marker parameters and actual image requests so the oracle exercises the vision path.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes: DeepSeek-V4 Flash Vision weight updates can complete across level-2 sleep/wake while preserving explicitly selected parameters omitted by the sender. Sending new values for those parameters still updates them with the retention configuration enabled. There is no new public API or CLI option; callers use the existing `--sleep-preserve-parameter-names` option with served-model names. A release-note fragment records the bug fix.

Weightless normalization tensors become nonpersistent buffers. The sentinel table now performs a small stack/cast on each execution; no performance improvement is claimed.

### How was this patch tested?

One physical Ascend NPU (device 3), TP=1, BF16; DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp reduced to **4 text layers, 2 vision layers and 8 experts**, maximum length 1024, memory utilization 0.45, block size 32. Model Runner V2 uses `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, capture size 1; the no-graph control uses `NONE`. Vision encoder graphs are disabled in both runs.

The transfer payload consists of deterministic fixed-seed checkpoint-compatible test tensors. An independent reference server loads the same tensors normally from safetensors; this checks transfer correctness rather than pretrained-model accuracy. Environment: Python 3.12.13, torch 2.10.0+cpu, torch-npu 2.10.0.post4, Transformers 5.14.1, triton-ascend 3.2.2 and CANN 9.1.0. Both packages are editable installs pointing to their corresponding source trees.

```bash
source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
source /path/to/venv/bin/activate
cd /path/to/vllm-ascend
export VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1
export VLLM_RL_TEST_DEVICE_INDEX=3
export VLLM_RL_DSV4_MODEL=/path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp
export VLLM_RL_DSV4_TEXT_LAYERS=4 VLLM_RL_DSV4_VISION_LAYERS=2
export VLLM_RL_DSV4_EXPERTS=8 VLLM_RL_DSV4_MEM_UTIL=0.45
unset VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER VLLM_RL_DSV4_SKIP_SLEEP VLLM_RL_DSV4_HASH_LAYERS \
  VLLM_RL_DSV4_RESET_MM_CACHE VLLM_RL_DSV4_DUMMY_TEXT_ONLY \
  VLLM_RL_DSV4_CUDAGRAPH_MODE VLLM_RL_DSV4_MM_ENCODER_GRAPH
test_file=tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/rlhf/state_transitions/test_npu_ipc_weight_transfer_dsv4_flash_vision.py
python -m pytest -sv "$test_file"

VLLM_RL_DSV4_CUDAGRAPH_MODE=NONE VLLM_RL_DSV4_MM_ENCODER_GRAPH=0 \
  python -m pytest -sv -k test_retention_with_vision_reload "$test_file"
```

The related unit run covered:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v4_moe.py \
  tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v4_vision.py \
  tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v4_vision_preprocess.py \
  tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v4_weight_loader_reload.py \
  tests/ut/worker/test_sleep_parameter_retention.py \
  tests/ut/worker/test_worker_v1.py \
  tests/ut/distributed/weight_transfer/test_npu_ipc_engine.py \
  tests/ut/distributed/weight_transfer/test_packed_tensor.py
```

#### Result

| Local validation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Full update + retention, FULL_DECODE_ONLY, packed/unpacked | 4 passed, zero errors/skips/failures (878.346 s) |
| Retention, NONE, packed/unpacked | 2 passed, zero errors/skips/failures (521.997 s) |
| Related model, loader, Worker, IPC and packed transport unit tests | 253 passed, zero errors/skips/failures |
| Mypy on the four modified production modules and consolidated vision test, Python 3.10/3.11/3.12 | Passed for all three targets |
| Complete repository format check | `bash format.sh ci`: passed, all hooks |

The hardware runs used production/test commit `97458f9fdc8979b0c9940b775fcb5d8ed13c53d3`; source SHA256 manifests bind the results to those files. Any subsequent release-note-only commit leaves those tested files unchanged. GitHub CI results are separate from these local results.

Four retention evidence JSON files cover **12 selected parameters**: 3 `tid2eid`, 4 `bias_vl`, 1 `e_score_correction_bias` and 4 `attn_sink`. Each checks two distinct current-value states, CPU backup hashes, restored device values and unchanged storage addresses at start/finalize/finish boundaries and after KV-cache wake. Test-only poisoning happens after allocator remapping and before Worker restores CPU copies. Probes resolve native meta placeholders to the retained kernel parameter and account for shared aliases.

The controls verify trainer-supplied new values with preservation still enabled, full updates after disabling preservation and level-1 sleep. Text/image output and token logprobs match independent normal-startup references. Native CPU reload regressions reproduced duplicate shared-module accounting and suppression of supplied new values before the fixes. The standard weights pool released about 26.96 GiB in the full-update reduced-model lane; other retained/update runs vary with their allocation state. This is a lifecycle observation, not a memory benchmark.

#### Regression scope

- The NPU IPC completion change affects models using `sleep_preserve_parameter_names`; the empty-pattern path continues through native initialization/finalization. Other model families were not hardware-tested. Packed/unpacked transport itself is unchanged.
- No new process-global reload skip rules or meta-materialization override is installed. Selected omitted parameters participate in native loader accounting; parameters already supplied by the trainer are not replaced by retained values.
- Normalization tests cover original-object/value preservation, nonpersistent state, repeated registration and dtype conversion. IPC tests cover shared modules, shared parameters, repeated current values, stable addresses and supplied-value precedence. Vision tests verify updated marker values and the native processor interface.
- Git merge compatibility against official main `33746f6e0810c0c2886a6fafde1b9ba9ced47ed7` was checked cleanly. Hardware results apply to the historical base plus the tested implementation, not the synthetic merge tree.
- Full-size checkpoints, pretrained-weight accuracy, FP8, multi-card/HCCL, vision-encoder graphs and broad performance benchmarks were not run. Retention tests require a vLLM revision exposing the existing retention field and explicitly skip on older versions; the recorded runs had zero skips.
- Dependency/deprecation warnings, native `Failed to load weights` fallback warnings for `AscendRMSNorm`, `ComplexExpRotaryEmbedding`, `AscendDeepseekSparseAttention` and `AscendUnquantizedFusedMoEMethod`, and producer-shutdown IPC warnings remain visible in logs. Functional assertions passed; the two hardware logs recorded 476 HTTP responses, all 200. Four evidence files retain the parameter and generation checks.
- **vLLM base used for local validation:** [c4df37dfcc7f72ca41cd43801a468526ecf99a2b](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c4df37dfcc7f72ca41cd43801a468526ecf99a2b), with no local vLLM source changes. CI-selected version metadata is reported separately.
- **vllm-ascend base:** official upstream main commit [19c2f7a7cb1504d4624620ea59d6c7fa9eadc422](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/commit/19c2f7a7cb1504d4624620ea59d6c7fa9eadc422), including #18838. The source branch starts directly from this commit.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: Packed/unpacked, shared module/parameter aliases, hash/non-hash routing, two current-value states, omitted and supplied retained parameters, full update and level-1 controls.
- [x] **Regression test**: Native reload tests reproduce incorrect shared-module accounting and dropped trainer-supplied new values; model tests cover normalization state, marker freshness and processor compatibility.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: No hardware timeout or transport-failure injection was performed.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: Real CPU backup hashes, NPU values, storage addresses and text/image logprobs against independent startup references.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: No broad benchmark or performance regression measurement; the per-forward marker stack/cast cost and validation limits are documented above.

items.title: [Feature][AI QoS] Support per-domain collective communication priority
items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

On Ascend A5, collective-communication domains (TP, DP, the default world group, weight transfer, and so on) share the same link. This PR lets each HCCL domain be created with its own QoS priority so those flows can be scheduled separately.

The feature is off by default. Turn it on with `additional_config.ai_qos` or `--ai-qos`. Priorities are `low` / `medium` / `high`, mapped to HCCL QoS 2 / 4 / 6. RDMA traffic class is `qos * 32`. A domain not listed in `manual` uses `default_priority` (`medium`).

QoS is applied when the communicator is created:

- Process groups such as TP and DP receive it through `hccl_config`.
- The default world group receives it from a wrapper around `init_process_group`, under the name `default_world`.
- Weight transfer receives it through `HcclCommInitRootInfoConfig`, under the name `weight_transfer`.
- Netloader's stateless process group receives it through `pg_options.hccl_config`.

Only A5 (`ascend950`) builds and uses this path. Other devices keep the previous communicator initialization. `manual` keys must be the normalized group name: the suffix after the first `:` is dropped, and `p_tp_*` is folded into `p_tp`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes.

- New CLI flag `--ai-qos '<json>'`. It is merged into `additional_config["ai_qos"]`. Specifying both `--ai-qos` and `additional_config.ai_qos` is an error.
- New config block `ai_qos.collective_communication`. Defaults: `enabled=false`, `default_priority="medium"`, `manual={}`. When `enabled` is true, groups listed in `manual` use that priority; every other group uses `default_priority`.

Example:

```bash
--ai-qos '{"collective_communication":{"enabled":true,"default_priority":"medium","manual":{"tp":"low","pp":"medium","pcp":"high","dcp":"low"}}}'
```

When `enabled` is true, every HCCL domain on A5 gets a priority, including domains omitted from `manual`.

### How was this patch tested?

Launched a model with the new command-line QoS configuration and verified the applied priority in hcomm by adding logs.

1. **Use upstream loading primitives.** HF names are translated by vLLM `WeightsMapper`; a streaming generator expands fused expert tensors. Packed IPC accumulates chunks and calls `load_weights` once per complete update, before native `finalize_layerwise_reload`. Unpacked IPC keeps its existing loading path.
2. **Use Worker buffer and parameter restoration.** Existing RoPE buffers use the native level-2 buffer backup. 3. **Retain current checkpoint-backed values explicitly.** `tid2eid`, `bias_vl`, `e_score_correction_bias` and `attn_sink` use the existing `--sleep-preserve-parameter-names` option when the sender omits them. They are not automatically frozen: full updates still replace their values. Vision/correction biases have deterministic zero defaults for dummy startup.
4. **Keep native sleep memory behavior.** The normal CaMem weights pool releases physical memory and remaps the reserved virtual addresses on wake. Ordinary allocator cache is cleared before remapping. No persistent weights pool is added.
5. **Invalidate the vision sentinel cache at its owner.** `load_weights` clears the concatenated marker cache so subsequent image forwards use current marker values. HF processor call compatibility and the upstream PCP helper relocation are handled at their existing call sites.
6. **Limit the reload patch to accounting exclusions.** The small compatibility patch updates upstream skip sets in place for runtime buffers/shared aliases. Exclusion alone neither freezes nor preserves parameter values. There is no global meta-materialization override or zero-fill wrapper; the patch registry explains its removal condition.

RoPE implementations, the HCCL engine, production environment variables and unrelated shared test matrices are restored to the historical base. Full-update and retention integration tests share one standalone vision module.

No new public Python API or CLI option. Frozen-parameter callers must select served-model names using the existing retention option and omit those parameters from the sender payload. Normal sleep can release the weights pool; retained parameters and runtime buffers still require CPU backups.

labels.description: run selected e2e test for pr

items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

EPLB creates receive buffers through `torch.empty_like` on `EplbExpertTensorList`. On ACLNN-only devices, that call can silently convert expert weights stored in an internal NPU format such as NZ (`FRACTAL_NZ_C0_16`) into ND buffers. The resulting weight/buffer format mismatch breaks the expert-transfer path.

This PR:

- reads the source tensor's NPU format with `torch_npu.get_npu_format`;
- allocates the EPLB buffer with `torch_npu.empty_with_format` when dtype, layout, device, and preserve-format semantics are unchanged;
- keeps the existing `torch.empty_like` behavior for non-NPU tensors or calls that request different tensor properties.

This PR intentionally contains only the EPLB buffer-allocation fix. It does not include the separate internal-format `copy_` workaround.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API change. EPLB receive buffers now preserve the storage format of their source expert weights on Ascend NPU.

### How was this patch tested?

- `ruff check vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/routed_experts.py`
- `ruff format --check vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/routed_experts.py`
- `git diff --check`
- NPU smoke validation confirmed that an NZ source weight and its newly allocated EPLB buffer both use format 50; before this fix the buffer was created as format 2 (ND).

CPU unit tests mock the NPU allocator and cover per-expert ACL format propagation, `requires_grad`, standard `empty_like` fallbacks, rejection of nonzero source storage offsets, and rejection of source/buffer stride mismatches. The existing NPU smoke validation covers the real ACLNN-only allocation behavior.

items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds exact MoE expert offload to enable `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` to run on a single Ascend 950PR or 950DT device when its full weights exceed NPU memory capacity.

Prepared target routed-expert weights and scales are stored in pinned host memory. Router-selected experts are loaded into stable per-layer NPU slots without changing routing, dropping experts, or substituting expert weights. Prefill, mixed batches, and decode capacity overflow use a reusable full-expert pool.

- Support Model Runner V2 (MRV2) eager execution and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` ACL graphs, including replayed expert loading, capacity filtering, and transfer-failure handling.
- Support both synchronous and asynchronous scheduling. Offload execution and weight publication remain serialized per worker to preserve correctness.
- Reuse checkpoint loading and native W4A8 MXFP post-processing, preserving native NZ weight and scale layouts.
- Support checkpoint-native DSpark with eager drafting and fixed verification. Only target routed experts are offloaded; draft experts remain fully resident on the NPU and follow the existing loading and execution paths.
- Add unit tests, native-copy/graph tests, and real MRV2/checkpoint integration tests. Both E2E test files are registered in `curated_tests.a5`, with the directory routed to `a5-4` by default.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Yes. Expert offload is disabled by default. Enable it through Ascend additional configuration, for example:

```bash
--additional-config '{"expert_offload_config":{"enabled":true,"num_device_experts":84}}'
```

`num_device_experts` controls target resident slots per layer and must satisfy `top_k <= num_device_experts < num_experts`. The current adapter requires W4A8 MXFP routed experts with group size 32. Compatibility is checked against each layer's capabilities and tensor layout; full-model validation covers `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`.

The implementation requires MRV2 and single-worker execution: TP/DP/PP/PCP/DCP sizes must all be one. Use eager execution or compilation mode `NONE` with `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`. Both scheduler modes are supported. Checkpoint-native DSpark additionally requires eager drafting, fixed verification, and `max_num_seqs=1`.

EP/EPLB, DBO, LoRA, sleep/wake, online weight reloading, generic CPU weight offload, and PD disaggregation are outside the current support scope. This PR does not add expert prefetch, hot-expert preload, bounded pinned staging, or allocator prewarm.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Functional coverage

- 875 unit tests passed across expert offload, DSpark, DeepSeek MoE, and existing runner regression coverage.
- Native expert-copy/compute/graph tests and the real MRV2/checkpoint integration test passed on A5. Integration coverage includes checkpoint loading and finalization, prefill, graph decode, eager fallback when expert capacity is exceeded, comparison with an offload-disabled reference, and cleanup.
- The DSpark target/draft lifecycle integration test also passed on A5.

#### Accuracy

Previous full-model GPQA validation used 198 questions. The single-card expert-offload deployment matched the four-card colocated reference:

| Deployment | Correct answers | Accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Single-card expert offload | 183 / 198 | 92.42% |
| Four-card colocated reference | 183 / 198 | 92.42% |

The four-card result is an accuracy reference; expert offload in this PR remains a single-worker feature.

#### Representative performance

Single-card `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, batch size/concurrency 1, 65,536 input tokens, 1,024 output tokens, and an actual aggregate prefix-cache hit rate of 90%:

| Metric | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Mean time to first token (TTFT) | 13.60 s |
| Mean time per output token (TPOT) | 40.22 ms/token |
| Mean end-to-end request latency | 54.75 s |
| Aggregate output throughput, including prefill | 18.70 tokens/s |

These measurements use five sequential requests after warmup, with profiling disabled. Timing uses the offline LLM interface and excludes HTTP frontend overhead. Throughput is total generated tokens divided by total request wall time.

The configuration uses 84 resident target experts per layer, a fully resident draft, DSpark with 5 speculative tokens, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, a 262,144-token context limit, a 3 GiB FP8 KV-cache budget, block size 32, and `max_num_batched_tokens=2048`. The benchmark environment includes a separate per-group draft KV block-size compatibility fix, which is outside this offload PR.

These are representative results, not the best achievable performance. Additional performance optimizations have not yet been upstreamed and are outside the scope of this PR.

items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Reduce RFork loading overhead and support DeepSeek V4.1 and MTP loading with **vLLM v0.31.0**, matching `.github/vllm-release-tag.commit`. The `vLLM main` footer identifies the separate verified main CI baseline.

This PR is specifically targeted at **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DSV4.1-Flash)**: the tensor scan deduplication, seed lifecycle, Engram host-weight loading, and MTP metadata handling below were adapted and validated for the DSV4.1-Flash main model together with its MTP draft model.

- **Tensor traversal and registration:** Deduplicate shared-object scans with layered BFS and deterministic tensor IDs. Reuse registration inventories, NPU formats, and layout digests while preserving registered parameter/buffer paths and rejecting ambiguous container labels.
- **Seed lifecycle:** Refresh registrations and manifests after post-load reshapes without changing the checkpoint-layout seed key. Reject processed-layout publication after structural drift. Support legacy planner leases, retry failed allocation returns, and retain published memory until withdrawal and cleanup are safe.
- **Engram and MTP:** Load Engram host tables locally before NPU registration or shared draft reuse, track ownership, and release discarded tables before fallback. Prepare MTP head ownership and aliases using the vLLM 0.31 four-field checkpoint metadata contract. Exclude locally derived RoPE caches from transfer.
- **Configuration and coverage:** Add optional readable planner identity headers, expand regression coverage, and synchronize the English/Chinese guide.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes.

**Compatibility and local weights**

Seed and receiver must use compatible RFork code, tensor IDs, and tensor/alias graphs. Compatibility with legacy planners does not provide interoperability with old workers: planners must match the full opaque `SEED_KEY`, and `SEED_RANK` remains required.

Engram host tables and process-local UVA pointers are not transferred. Each receiver needs the matching indexed safetensors checkpoint, including host weights and scales. Existing topology restrictions remain in effect. MTP metadata preparation failures fall back to ordinary loading without publishing a seed.

**Planner configuration**

| Option in `--model-loader-extra-config` | Default | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rfork_model_identity_headers` | `false` | Attach readable model metadata to planner requests. Explicit JSON booleans override `RFORK_MODEL_IDENTITY_HEADERS`, which accepts `0/1/false/true`, ignoring case and surrounding whitespace. Invalid values fail initialization; enabled header values must be ASCII. |
| `rfork_seed_removal_supported` | `false` | Skip removal requests by default. Use `true` for a confirmed removal contract, or `null` for automatic detection. An unknown `404` in automatic mode does not confirm withdrawal. |

Legacy planners need no renewal, removal, expiry, or draining extensions. Unconfirmed withdrawal retains registered memory until safe cleanup or process exit. See the [RFork guide](https://github.com/yangsonglin13/vllm-ascend/blob/rfork_bugfix_0923/docs/source/user_guide/feature_guide/rfork.md) for protocol and configuration details.

**Known limitation — Engram shared-memory fallback**

With `dp_shared_memory=true`, fallback is not coordinated across the sharing group. If only some ranks encounter a seed miss or registration/transfer failure, rebuilding their shared tables can hang startup. This remains unresolved; successful shared-memory execution does not validate this failure path.

### How was this patch tested?

**CPU regression coverage**

- **351 passed, 1 deselected**, with external vLLM/NPU dependencies stubbed where needed. Coverage includes tensor IDs, scan/registration reuse, publication, planner leases and shutdown races, configuration, MTP metadata, Engram ownership/loading/cleanup, and RoPE cache exclusion.
- The MTP metadata regression reproduces the three-versus-four-field unpacking failure and checks selected checkpoint files, secondary-source prefixes, and unsupported/corrupt/empty/missing metadata. An isolated probe using the vLLM 0.31 method and a real safetensors file also passed, with external runtime and checkpoint-filter dependencies stubbed.

```text
python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/ut/model_loader/rfork tests/ut/model_loader/rfork --ignore=tests/ut/model_loader/rfork/test_rfork_loader.py --ignore=tests/ut/model_loader/rfork/test_transfer_backend.py -k "not test_configured_seed_port_falls_back_when_already_in_use" -q --tb=short
```

The two loader/backend test files were excluded from this local run. The deselected case tests a Windows socket conflict; Linux is the supported deployment platform.

**Static checks**

Ruff check/format, import and boolean-context checks, package initialization, symbolic-meta, long-function, filename/logger checks, release-fragment YAML parsing, and diff whitespace checks passed for the latest fix. Earlier integration checks also reported Markdown lint, codespell, typos, and redacted Gitleaks scans passing. The full manual pre-commit run passed.

**Hardware evidence and remaining validation**

Engram shared-memory execution passed in user-reported testing. Full RFork loader/backend integration, NPU inference, Engram UVA execution, and sleep recovery were not validated on this host. Final-HEAD NPU inference and controlled performance measurements were validated on the target hardware.

Historical DSV4.1-Flash + MTP logs, averaged over 8 TP ranks, showed:

| Metric | Baseline | Optimized | Observed reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `register_memory_region` internal timer | 43.72 s | 0.67 s | 98.5% |
| Complete destination registration, including digest binding | 90.84 s | 1.87 s | 97.9% |
| Main-model RFork load | 374.72 s | 192.23 s | 48.7% |
| MTP draft-model RFork load | 11.00 s | 4.45 s | 59.5% |
| Main-model weight read | 2.26 s | 2.30 s | Approximately unchanged |

Both runs used `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` / `DeepSeekV4MTPModel`, TP=8, PP=1, DP=1, and expert parallelism, with `source=transfer` for main and draft models. Each main-model rank covered 2,638 tensors and 34.92 GiB of logical weights. The internal registration timer is narrower than the complete registration stage; model-load timings do not measure server readiness. These are single runs from an earlier optimization revision on different machine/planner environments, not final-HEAD or controlled same-host benchmarks.

### Checklist

- [x] Boundary, regression, and failure-path coverage.
- [x] CPU tensor/checkpoint tests with external runtime dependencies isolated.
- [x] Complete manual pre-commit run.
- [x] Full loader/backend integration and final-HEAD NPU inference validation.
- [x] Controlled final-HEAD NPU performance comparison.

items.title: [BugFix][EPLB] Complete MRv1 AllGather redundant expert routing and migration
items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #19915.

A2 MRv1 ALLGATHER needs each route to execute once and hot-expert tokens to use multiple copies. This patch keeps the existing planner and P2P transfer, and adds:

- Consistent per-row replica selection across ranks, with ownership based on current physical slots.
- Load counts for actual, valid local routes, excluding padding.
- In-place routing refresh after weights/scales migrate, including replica reassignment and graph replay.

Related: #17406, #19861, #18549. Credit to the [#19861 review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/19861#discussion_r4384186295) for the ownership issue; its latest head already fixes that part. This patch also covers token sharing, changing hot experts and real migration.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes: A2 MRv1 ALLGATHER can use dynamic redundant experts with existing settings. Validated on four cards with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B W8A8, TP4/EP4, SwiftBalance, eight redundant experts and FULL_DECODE_ONLY. Release note included.

### How was this patch tested?

- CPU module regressions: **116 passed, 11 skipped** (CPU fixtures; prepare/finalize fixture matched the runtime image).
- Four-card regression: **passed**; two layers, changing hotspots, padding/empty rows, actual P2P weight/scale migration and graph replay:
  ```bash
  VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 pytest -q tests/e2e/pull_request/four_card/test_allgather_eplb.py
  ```
- Full model: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B W8A8 on four Ascend 910B2C cards; exact-answer checks **8/8**, 133 weight-update cycles; MTP with three draft tokens also passed **8/8** and migrated all 41 layers.
- Single-variable benchmark: redundancy 0 → 8, same model/code/hardware; GSM8K first 32 test questions, concurrency 8, fixed 256 output tokens/question, warm-up then two rounds, heat/algorithm intervals 600/50. Median throughput **311.1 → 318.9 token/s (+2.5%)**. With the same fixed-output workload at high-frequency intervals 30/10, throughput was **170.4 → 252.2 token/s (+48.0%)**. Native NPU profiling showed reduced rebalance-related waiting rather than faster expert GEMM; the larger gain is specific to frequent rebalancing.

Hardware runs used CANN 9.2.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post7, vLLM `ced6857a`, and Ascend image `8fde6d4e` overlaid with the changed source files. Ruff and CI test mapping passed; full Linux CI remains to run.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: empty/partial batches, padding, multiple layouts.
- [x] **Regression test**: each route executes once before/after migration.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: missing experts and unequal rank capacity.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: numerical outputs, real migration and graph replay.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: manual benchmark above; no automated performance threshold.

items.title: [Feature][Spec Decode] Support Kimi K3 GQA DSpark with DCP
items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable a Kimi K3 target with decode context parallelism and a replicated GQA DSpark draft on Ascend Model Runner V2. Rebased onto `484cd036c923aba3d51d24e45ee89817a020d9da`, paired with verified vLLM `c0b6f74bee518aeaf5d72b200a0216e72fbb5e7c`.

The paired vLLM already includes [927c87b3472a](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/927c87b3472a39da79a95a8df12d0a2b21e2d32e). This PR reuses upstream draft DCP=1 and the per-group `dcp_sharded` flag. Ascend slot mapping, metadata, scheduler block spans, prefix lookup, cache pools and Mooncake transfers now respect that flag. No new user flag is required.

Dense draft K/V requires contiguous physical pools alongside the hybrid target/Mamba storage. The allocation patch separates those pools and delegates their descriptors to the upstream planner; its removal condition is documented in `vllm_ascend/patch/__init__.py`. DCP MLA execution and graph updates reuse the FIA V2 implementation already on main; regression tests cover strided hybrid pages and padded mixed-length batches.

Full-weight testing on 950 also exposed four failures in the documented K3 configuration:

- The fused O-projection returns a sequence shard, so the decoder must skip its second ReduceScatter.
- Native S8S4 grouped matmul requires packed ND weights and 256-channel scale groups. K3's per-channel W4A8 Situ path now uses zero-stride scale views and the existing unfused Situ pipeline. Unsupported expert-weight lists fail early.
- Prepared KDA state-copy launches omitted constexpr argument slots retained by Triton 3.6; the compiled launch now preserves that ABI, as the existing fallback already does.
- The integer shared-expert fusion called `DequantSituQuant`, registered only for A2/A3. Devices without that capability now retain the registered linear and Situ implementations.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. K3 can combine target DCP with a GQA DSpark draft using existing parallel and speculative parameters. The full W4A8+QuaRot checkpoint passes generation in the configuration below. The independent empty-expert GMM fix has been extracted to [#19812](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/19812); this PR does not contain its guards, tests, or release note. Full-weight validation includes that prerequisite fix.

### How was this patch tested?

Full-weight test topology: four Ascend950DT hosts / 32 devices, DP4/TP8/EP32, target DCP2, draft DCP1/TP8, DSpark greedy K7, target `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, draft eager, prefix caching and FlashComm1. Target: all 347 shards, 93 layers and 896 experts; original five-layer BF16 GQA draft. No layer or expert reduction.

The launch uses the repository's 950 mixed-deployment topology/environment and adapts the K3 four-card smoke budgets: context 2048, batched tokens 512, four sequences, capture sizes `[16,32]`, block size 128. It retains full weights and a 0.9 memory budget rather than the A3 test's dummy weights/512 MiB KV cap. `HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE` is unset. Deprecated `--mamba-cache-mode` is omitted; paired upstream automatically selects K3's prefix-cache mode.

Frozen test snapshot `94e8d9ca0a93c3bdaa75177ba5c20271eba7ae21`, run `smoke-full-dcp2-r10`: **19/19 requests passed, 219 generated tokens**, covering completion/chat, four concurrent requests, 1/127/128/129/769/1537/1665-token boundaries, repeated prefix, and eight full-vocabulary logits exports. All four DP nodes replayed ACL graphs. Natural-language smoke accepted **55/196 draft tokens**. Four logits cases (eight steps, vocabulary 163840, fixed generated token IDs) are bitwise identical across repeats. **DCP1-versus-DCP2 comparison remains incomplete**: the DCP1 control exited before weight loading because other model processes occupied the four hosts (about 73–78 GB per device). No cross-DCP accuracy pass is inferred from repeat stability.

After the frozen run started, main advanced to `484cd036c`; the feature branch was rebased, retaining main's hardware applicability markers and this PR's slot-mapping reference coverage. The empty-expert fix was then removed from this branch and submitted separately as #19812. The frozen snapshot is retained for a same-source DCP1 control; it is not the current feature head in isolation.

Predeclared cross-DCP gates: relative L2 <= 0.01, cosine >= 0.9999, argmax agreement 100%, with explicit DP-rank routing and repeated controls.

Validation completed for the current fixes:

- Attention-residual reproduction: fused cases fail before the fix; all four cases pass afterward in eager and graph execution, with exact replay equality. The isolated test uses the production decoder method and native residual operator with simulated attention/collectives.
- W4A8: 38 repository unit tests and 16 source-harness cases pass. Actual checkpoint GMM1/GMM2 match an independent signed-INT4 unpack/dequant reference at `atol=rtol=0.02`. The production routed MLP passes one-expert, 28-expert and padded-capacity cases; graph replay exactly matches eager.
- Shared experts: 201 repository tests pass; 15 dependency-free contracts pass. Actual checkpoint TP8 shared-expert slices at 1/8/128 tokens match integrated execution and graph replay exactly. Against independent INT8 matmul/dequant and Situ reference, maximum relative L2 is 0.002369 and minimum cosine is 0.999997.
- KDA compiled-launch ABI: 64 native NPU tests pass; four optional native-reference cases skip because that reference build is not installed.
- Rebase checks: 10 focused source tests pass; retained main's uncached `is_dcp_enabled()` helper. `bash format.sh ci` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Separate 32-rank Gloo and HCCL+Gloo probes pass 16 rounds of broadcasts, all-reduces and barriers. Earlier intermittent Gloo initialization failures are retained in the experiment record; no networking workaround was added.

Runtime uses the 20261024 A5 image's native extensions/CANN custom assets with the stated paired Python/Triton revisions. This is not a full native rebuild or a performance benchmark. The supplied full checkpoint records a lossy MXFP4-to-BF16 conversion before W4A8 export; no equivalence to original prequantization BF16 is claimed.

Historical A3 evidence (Ascend `b4f8002`, vLLM `c4df37d`; reduced 5-layer/32-expert target, TP4): DCP1/2/4 functional suites passed 22 requests / 408 tokens each; DCP2 HTTP suite passed 21 requests / 336 tokens. DCP2/DCP4 target graph replay was observed on all ranks. Six native FIA regression cases and 83 MLA/DCP graph unit tests passed (three topology skips). These reduced-checkpoint runs accepted zero draft tokens and did not pass the tensor gate; the DCP1 repeat control also diverged, so those results do not establish numerical correctness of the full configuration.

items.title: [BugFix][EPLB] Wait for buffer consumption before HIXL reads
items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix a shared-buffer race in asynchronous HIXL EPLB. After the foreground queues the copy from `expert_buffer` into a layer's weights, `CpuGpuEvent.wait()` only enqueues its consumption wait on the EPLB stream. HIXL uses private streams, so the next layer's READ can overwrite the buffer before that copy finishes. Synchronizing after the READ cannot repair the overwritten data.

Remember the stream passed to `set_stream()` and synchronize it **before** starting HIXL READs, falling back to the current accelerator stream for synchronous callers. The synchronization remains inside `gpu_sync_allowed()` and the existing collective error-handling path. This synchronizes the EPLB stream rather than the whole device.

This addresses the weight corruption reproduced while investigating [the QWEN3_235B_PD_3_5K_1_5k MRV2 failure](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/38513241241). The original run reported 4.32% GSM8K accuracy and later failed performance warmup with HTTP 502. A same-cluster unpatched reproduction generated corrupted text after its first asynchronous expert migration; it was stopped rather than reported as a completed accuracy measurement.

The patch is based on main `9d9682169c522b5028eb648179999f3d411f2c34`. It changes eight production lines and adds regression coverage; no model-runner, dependency-marker, benchmark threshold, timeout, or graph configuration changes are included.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Prevents expert-weight corruption when asynchronous EPLB reuses a HIXL receive buffer. No CLI, configuration, or public API changes.

### How was this patch tested?

**Real NPU regression and unit tests** (completed during the investigation; the four affected files are unchanged in main since that tested baseline):

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/ut/distributed/eplb/test_hixl_communicator.py tests/ut/distributed/eplb/test_hixl_compat.py
# 52 passed

python -m pytest -sv tests/e2e/pull_request/two_card/test_hixl_eplb_registration.py -k async_read_waits
# Unpatched: official-binding regression fails the consumed-weight assertion.
# Patched: 2 passed (official HIXL and ctypes fallback).

python -m pytest -sv tests/e2e/pull_request/two_card/test_hixl_eplb_registration.py -k main_and_draft_share
# 2 passed (existing shared-session sibling coverage).
```

The new two-NPU regression delays a foreground buffer copy while the EPLB stream waits on its consumption event, then starts the next layer's private HIXL READ. It checks both the previous layer's consumed weights and the new buffer contents. Unit coverage checks explicit-stream and current-stream ordering; existing failure-path tests exercise collective error propagation.

**Full original 48-NPU model workload**, keeping P DP2 x TP8, D DP32 x TP1, 1319 GSM8K questions, 760 performance requests, concurrency 190, and 1500 output tokens per performance request:

| Patched V2 run | GSM8K | Output token/s | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Full run 1 | 1272/1319 = 96.4367% | 3585.5705 | Both pass |
| Full run 2, coherent CANN runtime | 1264/1319 = 95.8302% | 3565.3294 | Both pass |

Accuracy baseline: 96.74%, absolute tolerance 2 percentage points. Throughput threshold: `3583.8747 * 0.97 = 3476.358459` output token/s. Each full run had 760 successful performance requests, zero failures, every output exactly 1500 tokens (1,140,000 total), and all three pytest processes exited 0. The second full run completed 10 real asynchronous EPLB migration cycles.

Invocation on each node, with the original case's cluster/model/dataset paths set for the test environment:

```bash
CONFIG_YAML_PATH=/path/to/QWEN3_235B_PD_3_5K_1_5k.yaml \
LWS_WORKER_INDEX=<0-or-1-or-2> BENCHMARK_HOME=/path/to/benchmark \
python -m pytest -sv tests/e2e/common/multi_node/external_dp/test_external_dp.py
```

Environment: A3, aarch64, Python 3.12.13, Torch 2.10.0+cpu, torch_npu 2.10.0.post4, triton-ascend 3.2.2, CANN 9.2.0. The full reproductions used the failing CI's actual Ascend `e7bf9c73b01d2a889db80a77868c0644f3d8b723` + vLLM `ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607` combination with this communicator fix. The original communicator is identical to main's. Host driver versions differ from CI.

**Validation boundaries:** main's pinned vLLM `c4df37dfcc7f72ca41cd43801a468526ecf99a2b` event contract was inspected, but that complete dependency combination has not undergone the full 235B run and remains a pre-merge validation item. This Windows checkout lacks Torch/vLLM, so the unit/NPU results above are the earlier Linux hardware runs, not a fresh Windows execution. Local static checks and pre-submit review are recorded below.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Integrate external FlashMLA decode, DSpark and DCP on #18256 at `ae45c77f70ebbe7d582dd14e8c43ddf1807418e8`. Preserve the dependency's separate, graph-stable decode/prefill current-KV workspaces, complete nonlocal prefill rows, query gathering, weight lifecycle and framework output/LSE merge. External metadata supplies live/padded history slots while the FlashMLA reader retains its fused paged cache.

The additional writer adapter addresses a device-observed layout rejection: a token-fused NoPE slice has token stride 576, while CANN's PROLOG writer requires 512 and permits only the outer page axis to be strided. For eligible external FlashMLA layers, allocate a bounded dense workspace after weight loading, run the existing PROLOG operator there, and scatter the written rows into the original history cache with the original slots. The same boundary covers DSpark context writes. It does not copy the history cache, replace the operator, alias DCP current-KV buffers, or alter the transport/collectives.

This is a stacked **draft awaiting device validation**. The integration-only delta is two commits above the pinned dependency; the main-targeted PR view also includes unmerged dependency changes.

The pinned dependency now preserves complete DCP prefill current rows and keeps decode/prefill workspaces disjoint. items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

A short prefill can be classified as decode while still loading external KV. MLA's prefill-only connector waits left decode paths uncovered. A pure-MLA decode step can skip load submission entirely and return incorrect output with HTTP 200. In a hybrid model, a completed layer load could remain unconsumed until a subsequent load hit the `thread: <layer_id> load failed` assertion and terminated the engine.

Complete the connector waits separately in the existing preprocessing paths:
- Native preprocessing and strided-cache fallback wait **after Q/KV projections**, preserving their overlap with KV transfer, and before KVPP synchronization or cache access. This wait also covers decode-classified short prefills.
- PROLOG_V3 waits once before its first decode or prefill cache access. Remove its later prefill-only wait so mixed batches consume the completion only once.
- Fused-only decode waits immediately before its KVPP hook and fused preprocessing.

Ordinary decode also records the attention-compute start boundary before its attention operator, matching prefill/external FlashMLA. This releases gated prefetches for subsequent layers; adding only load waits would otherwise block on layer 1.

Each selected path consumes the existing connector/PoolWorker completion once. Shared transfer/event cleanup code and request classification are unchanged.

Main counterpart of #19635 (releases/v0.30.0).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Fixes incorrect output and possible engine shutdowns when an MLA short prefill loads external KV through a layerwise connector. Existing native projection/transfer overlap is preserved. No configuration changes.

### How was this patch tested?

- Main's preceding wait-placement revision passed **65 CPU tests**. At the user's request, the new hardware validation and the two new decode-boundary regression cases were run on **releases/v0.30.0 only** (142 tests passed there); no further main tests were run.
- Ruff lint/format and `git diff --check` passed on this main revision. Full format-script execution remains blocked by actionlint hook installation/network access.
- **Main has not been tested on NPU.** The following is supporting evidence from release PR #19635, not a main-branch pass claim.

Real-NPU before/after validation on **releases/v0.30.0 only**, fixed commit `611ed038be00ffd685cf759c5e96cb8063c48b1f`:
- Ascend A3, TP=1, eager execution, real AscendStoreConnector + Memcache layerwise SDMA transfers. Image tag: `nightly-ci-releases-v0.30.0-a3-openeuler-cann9.2.0_20261022115200-20261023-r31`.
- Full **GLM-4.7-Flash-w8a8** weights, 47 MLA layers. A 257-token synthetic prompt hits 256 external KV tokens, leaving one row classified as decode (no speculative decoding configured). Between requests, reset local prefix cache with `reset_external=false`; run four unrelated prompts to overwrite local pages, then a 272-token/16-row prefill control and five identical short requests. Sampling: temperature=0, seed=0, max_tokens=1, logprobs=5.
- Identical non-mutating Python call/return observers in both runs record MLA metadata, PoolWorker waits and receiver copy results.

| GLM cached short requests | Original code | Fixed code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP status | 200, 5/5 | 200, 5/5 |
| Layer waits / completed KV copies per request | 0 / 0 | 47 / 47 |
| Output matches cold-cache reference | 0/5 | 5/5 |
| Returned logprobs match cold-cache reference exactly | 0/5 | 5/5 |
| Completion event still set after a load wait returns | No load waits occurred | 0 |

Cold output is `" river"`. Original cached outputs are `" "`, `" best"`, `" "`, `" code"`, `"orem"`; fixed outputs are all `" river"`. The ordinary 16-row prefill control completes 47 waits and 47 copies on both versions. This GLM run reproduces silent incorrect output, rather than an engine crash.

The first hardware attempt with waits but without the ordinary decode attention-start signal blocked on layer 1: layer 0 completed, while subsequent prefetched copies waited on the unopened attention gate. Adding `record_attention_compute_start()` before ordinary decode attention resolves that block.

This is targeted eager-mode lifecycle/one-token consistency validation, not a benchmark or a full accuracy evaluation. That initial run did not cover graph capture/replay, speculative decoding, TP>1 or a full-size Kimi deployment; the later full-model check below covers TP16/PP2.

Additional **minimal hybrid control-flow reproduction**, on the same v0.30.0 image/hardware:
- Four-layer KimiLinear architecture: KDA layers 0–2 followed by MLA layer 3; hidden_size=1024, 8 attention heads, head_dim=128, q_lora_rank=512, kv_lora_rank=512; `--load-format dummy --dtype bfloat16`, no MoE. This runs real NPU kernels and real Memcache transfers with random weights. It is not full-size Kimi model validation or a meaningful model accuracy test.
- Hybrid cache alignment selects block_size=512. A 513-token request hits 512 external tokens and leaves one decode-classified row. Use the same cold/local-reset/unrelated-prompts/16-row-prefill-control sequence as above.
- **Original:** first cached short request performs 4 successful copies but only 3 layer waits (KDA), leaving MLA layer 3 unconsumed. The second cached short request naturally raises `AssertionError: thread: 3 load failed` in `_copy_gva_layers`. EngineCore exits, HTTP 500 is returned, and the API process shuts down.
- **Fixed:** 5/5 cached short requests return HTTP 200, with 4 waits and 4 successful copies per request; no completion event remains set after a normal wait. No assertion occurs, and final `/health` is HTTP 200. Returned one-token text/logprobs also match that run's cold reference.
- No events, load tasks, or kernel results were injected or manually set. The observer only records production call/return state.

#### Fixed reduced-model streaming performance (v0.30.0 only)

Follow-up on fixed release commit `611ed038be00ffd685cf759c5e96cb8063c48b1f`, using the same four-layer random-weight KDA+MLA model, r31 image, TP=1 and eager configuration. The diagnostic observer was removed from PYTHONPATH and its trace environment variable was absent in the API process.

- Streaming HTTP completions: 513 input tokens, exactly 128 output tokens, temperature=0, seed=0, ignore_eos=true; return token IDs to verify complete output sequences.
- **120/120 measured requests succeeded** across six cases (20 each), plus 11 warmup requests. Every measured request returned HTTP 200, finished with 128 tokens, and matched its corresponding cold-warmup token sequence exactly.
- No server ERROR, assertion, EngineDeadError or repeated load-wait warning. Final health check returned HTTP 200.
- Cache restoration was verified against scheduler logs: single-concurrency external reload loads 512 tokens in 20/20 requests; distinct-prefix concurrency-4 reload also loads 512 tokens in 20/20 requests. Identical-prefix concurrency-4 requests share one restore per wave (5 restores for 20 requests), so a distinct-prefix case was added.
- Throughput below is aggregate output tokens per active request-window second, excluding deliberate cache-reset HTTP calls and reset sleeps. TTFT and E2E are measured from each streaming HTTP request; E2E includes receipt of the completed stream.

| Case, 20 requests each | Concurrency | TTFT p50 / p95 (ms) | E2E p50 / p95 (s) | Output token/s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Local prefix cache | 1 | 24.1 / 25.2 | 1.127 / 1.165 | 112.5 |
| Local prefix cache, explicit concurrency-4 warmup | 4 | 42.1 / 43.3 | 1.282 / 1.293 | 397.4 |
| External reload, reset local cache before each request | 1 | 27.8 / 31.1 | 1.200 / 1.313 | 105.4 |
| External reload, four distinct prefixes, reset before each wave | 4 | 49.2 / 53.2 | 1.295 / 1.319 | 393.6 |

The first concurrency-4 local-cache case, before an explicit concurrency-4 warmup, had a first-wave latency spike: TTFT p95=3315.8 ms, E2E p95=4.607 s and throughput=260.0 output token/s. Those 20 requests remain in the 120-request record; the explicitly warmed repeat is reported separately above. The additional shared-prefix external case achieved 388.7 output token/s.

These are fixed-version, reduced-model measurements, **not a before/after performance-regression comparison**, full-model accuracy/performance validation or a graph-mode result. Other NPUs on the host were running unrelated jobs. Main was not exercised.

#### Full Kimi K3 two-node validation (v0.30.0; GPQA stopped early)

- Full W4A8 Kimi K3 checkpoint: **93 layers, 896 experts, 347 complete weight shards**; no layer/expert reduction or random weights. Two Atlas A3 hosts, 32 devices total, TP=16 and PP=2 (48/45 layers), eager execution, language-model-only, no speculative decoding.
- Same r31 image as above. Only `vllm_ascend/attention/mla_v1.py` is replaced by the release fix; no diagnostic observer or other production-code overlay.
- All 32 ranks loaded successfully, the HTTP service became healthy, and three basic chat smoke checks passed.
- Actual hybrid cache block size is 384 tokens. A 769-token synthetic input restores **768 external KV tokens**, leaving one decode-classified row. Reset only local prefix cache, overwrite local pages with four unrelated inputs, and run a 16-row prefill control before the repeated short requests.
- **3/3 external-cache requests returned HTTP 200 and matched all 64 generated token IDs and text against the cold reference. Chosen-token logprobs matched exactly (maximum absolute delta=0).** Scheduler logs independently confirm 768 tokens actually loaded for each request; final health was HTTP 200.

Of 78 nontruncated outputs, 76 were correct; this subset is completion-biased and is not a full-benchmark score. items.title: [Feature][AI QoS] Support request-level KV transfer priority
items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add request-level KV transfer priority so requests sharing a service can use different transfer priorities. Mooncake is the initial backend; the request interface can support additional backends.

Propagate priority through Store GET/PUT, ordinary PD READ, and layerwise PD WRITE, including proxy handoff. Handle request validation, asynchronous Store completion, and layerwise buffer lifetime. Align the FastAPI dependency range with the paired vLLM requirement.

This revision moves `QosPDPool` and `QosStorePool` into vLLM-Ascend and initializes each lane through upstream `TransferEngine.initialize(...)`. Custom Mooncake QoS helper modules and the custom initialization binding are no longer required. Requests select existing engines; they do not modify process environment variables. A shared startup lock protects per-engine configuration and restores the original environment on success and failure.

Request fields, priority mapping, peer-port routing, buffer ownership, and Store key semantics are preserved. Only the default Store lane contributes capacity. Mainline integration retains the backend PUT success contract and stops lookup/transfer activity before closing the QoS pool.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Adds opt-in `additional_config.ai_qos` configuration through vLLM's existing `--additional-config` option and the request field `kv_transfer_params.kv_priority`. Levels `low` / `medium` / `high` map to channel QoS `0` / `3` / `7`.

```bash
--additional-config '{"ai_qos":{"kv_transfer":{"enabled":true,"request_priority":true,"default_priority":"low","log":false}}}'
```

```json
{"kv_transfer_params":{"kv_priority":"high"}}
```

The former `--ai-qos` option is removed. Put its JSON value under the `ai_qos` key, alongside any existing additional configuration. Python callers use `additional_config={"ai_qos": ...}`. QoS settings are validated during platform configuration; JSON parsing uses vLLM's standard parser.

Invalid priorities return a client error. Explicit connector `qos_priority` conflicts with enabled request-level QoS. Existing behavior is preserved when disabled. No vLLM core patch is required.

items.title: [Feature] Support upstream preload on Ascend Model Runner V2 (ND)
items.body: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Adapt the persistent weight-cache mechanism introduced in [vLLM #54921](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54921) to Ascend. A preload daemon keeps processed weights in NPU memory, allowing subsequent engines to import them through NPU IPC instead of loading another copy from disk. This is an Ascend-only adaptation: no upstream vLLM source changes, new production CLI options, or new environment variables are introduced. It reuses upstream `vllm preload`, `--load-format ipc_cache`, configuration matching, request/retry handling, health endpoints, fallback policy, and daemon lifecycle. #### Main changes and files | File / component | Responsibility | | --- | --- | | New `vllm_ascend/model_loader/preload/__init__.py` | Register the Ascend subclass of the upstream IPC loader when the required daemon APIs are available. Leave ordinary loading unchanged on older supported vLLM versions. | | New `vllm_ascend/model_loader/preload/config.py` | Validate the initial supported scope and reject incompatible layouts, offloading, and shared-weight mutations. | | New `vllm_ascend/model_loader/preload/daemon.py` | Extend the upstream daemon with NPU binding, Ascend runtime initialization, spawn-safe general-plugin initialization, and NPU cache cleanup. | | New `vllm_ascend/model_loader/preload/transport.py` | Export/rebuild ND tensors with torch_npu IPC, retain views and shared storage, reject NZ storage, and count exported NPU storage without counting aliases twice. | | New `vllm_ascend/model_loader/preload/loader.py` | Extend the upstream loader with Ascend configuration checks, tensor binding, RoPE cache restoration, failed-construction cleanup, and copy-release synchronization. | | New `vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_preload.py` | Install focused, idempotent adapters for upstream platform checks, daemon entry points, tensor export, and shared-storage accounting. | | Existing platform / worker / ops files | Integrate device UUID and NPU memory APIs, external-weight/KV accounting, processed-weight handling, and guards against modifying daemon-owned zero-copy weights. | | New `tests/ut/model_loader/preload/` and existing worker tests | Cover registration, interface compatibility, IPC metadata, configuration rejection, cleanup, plugin initialization ordering, and memory/lifecycle guards. | | New `tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/model_runner_v2/preload/` | Provide real-NPU IPC regression tests and explicit model/HTTP acceptance tools. `runner.py` and `validate.py` compare disk, zero-copy, and copy; `validate_yarn.py` covers RoPE restoration; `serve_smoke.py` checks the public serving CLI/API. The full acceptance scripts are not automatically executed merely by placing them under this directory. | The integration primarily uses inheritance. The remaining patches cover upstream CUDA-specific binding. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Enable Ascend engines to use the existing preload interface with `zero_copy` (default) or `copy`. Initial validated scope: - Model Runner V2, non-quantized text Dense models, BF16/FP16, and ND weights. Both daemon and engine must explicitly set `weight_nz_mode=0`. - Qwen3-8B on one Ascend 910B4-1, TP=1, eager and V2 graph execution. - Zero-copy engine restarts reuse the same daemon. The daemon must outlive all zero-copy consumers; sleep/offload and in-place weight updates are disallowed for shared weights. - Copy consumers own independent weights after handoff; the daemon cache is released after the transfer. TP rank/shard design is inherited from upstream, but TP>1 is not validated here. NZ IPC, quantization, MoE, MLA/SFA, multimodal models, speculative decoding, V1, and PP/DP/EP are outside this initial scope. #### Example Use a vLLM revision with the required preload interfaces; the current older CI pins only receive ordinary-loading compatibility coverage. Start the daemon first: ```bash export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm preload \ --model /data/models/Qwen3-8B \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --max-model-len 2048 \ --enforce-eager \ --additional-config '{"weight_nz_mode":0}' \ --weight-cache-socket-dir /tmp/ascend-preload \ --weight-cache-health-host 127.0.0.1 \ --weight-cache-health-port 9001 ``` After `http://127.0.0.1:9001/health` returns HTTP 200, start the consumer in another shell: ```bash export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve /data/models/Qwen3-8B \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --max-model-len 2048 \ --max-num-seqs 8 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.55 \ --enforce-eager \ --additional-config '{"weight_nz_mode":0}' \ --load-format ipc_cache \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"socket_dir":"/tmp/ascend-preload","mode":"zero_copy","fallback":false}' ``` These are eager-mode examples. Graph execution was checked separately. Positive acceptance tests explicitly disable fallback so ordinary disk loading cannot hide an IPC failure. ### How was this patch tested? #### Environment and source provenance - One Ascend 910B4-1 (64 GB); only the allocated NPU was used. - Python 3.12.13, torch 2.10.0+cpu, torch_npu 2.10.0.post4, CANN 9.1.0, triton-ascend 3.2.2. - Hardware runs used the working tree, including five separately staged E2E additions/updates that are not yet in the committed PR diff. The two added bootstrap pytest cases belong to that pending test-harness update; they are not claimed as committed tests below. #### Unit and compatibility tests The same related UT suite covers preload, non-quantized linear processing, allocator behavior, worker lifecycle/weight updates, and device UUIDs: | Official vLLM revision | Result | Interpretation | | --- | --- | --- | | `7dc44a00161ace6f8ba7be2cc008f926e5a35fe2` | 149 passed | All related UT cases executed. | | CI-main `c0b6f74bee518aeaf5d72b200a0216e72fbb5e7c` | 147 passed, 2 skipped | Daemon interfaces absent; ordinary-loading compatibility, not full preload support. | | Release v0.31.0 `db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6` | 144 passed, 5 skipped | Additional query/budget APIs absent; ordinary-loading compatibility only. | The old revisions used separate environments sharing the container dependencies; this does not certify their complete CI images. Only tests that actually depend on missing APIs are skipped. #### Real-NPU and model validation - Real NPU IPC: **8 passed**, covering BF16/FP16 contiguous, transposed and offset views, repeated consumers, tied parameters/shared storage, and explicit NZ rejection. - A separate spawn probe also verified real general-plugin initialization, cold/preloaded entry, and repeated-entry idempotency; its two pytest cases are in the pending E2E update, not this committed diff. - Qwen3-8B: **12 complete engine runs passed** for BF16/FP16 ordinary ND and zero-copy, eager/graph, including five consecutive eager restarts under one BF16 daemon. Fixed seed=0, greedy decoding, four fixed prompts, 32 output tokens, exact token-ID comparison, `fallback=false`. - Supplemental BF16 copy eager/graph: **2 passed**; exact token match, daemon exported bytes dropped from 16,412,928,576 to zero, and the consumer retained independent weights and completed inference. - Zero-copy consumers reported zero newly allocated model-weight bytes; KV budgets matched the ordinary ND baselines. BF16 five-restart free-HBM drift was 471,040 bytes (about 0.45 MiB). - Earlier acceptance also checked daemon absence/timeouts, configuration mismatch, disk fallback, YaRN cache restoration, and the HTTP serving entry point. The normal ND shutdown control also showed upstream shutdown warnings; this PR does not claim warning-free teardown. Entry points for reproducing the IPC regression and full model acceptance are: ```bash python -m pytest -q \ tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/model_runner_v2/preload/test_npu_ipc.py python -m tests.e2e.pull_request.one_card.model_runner_v2.preload.validate \ --model /data/models/Qwen3-8B \ --output-dir /tmp/ascend-preload-validation ``` #### Observed startup timings | Configuration | Ordinary ND | Ready daemon + zero-copy consumer | Time saved | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | BF16 graph | 32.74 s | 28.25 s | 4.48 s | | FP16 eager | 27.27 s | 21.32 s | 5.95 s | | FP16 graph | 33.49 s | 29.65 s | 3.84 s | These are functional-regression observations, not a controlled repeated benchmark. They measure `LLM` construction, exclude the daemon's initial 46.60–47.09 s startup, and are sensitive to compilation/cache state. Benefits apply to subsequent consumer starts; starting a new daemon for every engine does not provide this saving. #### Checks and remaining work - `bash format.sh ci`, commit hooks, and `git diff --check`: passed. Formatting checks were rerun when preparing the latest commit; the UT/NPU results above are from the saved prior runs, not a new run at commit time. - High-utilization copy startup budgeting and zero-copy-to-disk fallback budget restoration remain follow-up work. Copy was validated at utilization=0.55; no claim is made about its high-utilization startup boundary. - The user documentation, release-note fragment, and final E2E harness organization are intentionally deferred in this draft and must be settled before presenting the feature as merge-ready. ### Checklist - [x] Boundary and failure coverage includes unsupported formats/configurations, shared views/aliases, missing APIs, timeouts, and cache mismatches. - [x] Regression coverage includes daemon plugin ordering/errors, failed model cleanup, and shared-weight/KV accounting. - [x] Relevant real-NPU and model acceptance results are recorded with their scope and limitations. - [ ] Add finalized public documentation and the release-note fragment before merge. - [ ] Resolve the pending E2E harness scope and run the applicable community CI jobs. - [ ] Complete controlled performance benchmarking if a guaranteed performance claim is required. - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c0b6f74bee518aeaf5d72b200a0216e72fbb5e7c --- Need help on this PR? items.title: [BugFix][PD] Recover backing storage for hybrid Mooncake V1 registration
items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Mooncake V1's hybrid-attention registration path takes the minimum logical tensor-view address and registers the descriptor size from that address. A view after allocation padding can fail the 2 MiB alignment check. Two descriptors sharing one allocation can also produce overlapping registrations, including a range extending beyond the allocation.

Reuse the existing storage-aware registration implementation, which already recovers aligned backing addresses, handles private layer allocations and coalesces overlaps. Keep logical layer addresses and block strides in the transfer metadata.

Related to #16632; this addresses the remaining V1 hybrid-attention branch, not the entire issue. The adjacent padded-span PR #16129 changes `mooncake_hybrid_connector.py`; this change is in `mooncake_connector.py`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No new API or configuration. Hybrid-attention V1 registration now accepts valid views after allocation padding and avoids overlapping registrations for shared backing storage.

### How was this patch tested?

- Four CPU regressions cover an unaligned logical view, aliases sharing one allocation, separate private layer allocations, and the `register_kv_caches()` entry point retaining logical transfer metadata.
- Against unmodified Ascend main `8c0667e52686602726e97972f9b19704d20d4411`: all four regressions fail.
- With this patch, the complete Mooncake V1 unit file passes: **192 passed, 14 existing skipped**.
- Tests use real vLLM Python code at the verified commit below and the repository's CPU UT mocks for accelerator/platform startup boundaries.
- A separate Ascend 910B3 allocation-address smoke passes the unaligned-view and shared-backing cases using the production registration methods and real NPU storage. This is not a Mooncake/HCCL transfer or model-serving test.
- Full repository `bash format.sh ci` passed, including Ruff, codespell, typos, workflow lint and the staged secret scan. `git diff --check` passed.
- Real two-card Ascend 910B3 P/D functional smoke passed with **Gemma 3 1B IT**, real model weights, eager BF16, TP=1 per engine, prefix caching disabled, 128-token blocks, max length 2048 and 256 MiB KV budget per engine. Both engines registered six sliding-window groups plus one full-attention group, exercising the V1 hybrid-attention branch without a Mamba group.
- Three prompts of **6, 14 and 1088 tokens** each generated 32 tokens. Direct Decode generation and Prefill-to-Decode generation had **identical token IDs in all three cases**. Decode logs recorded successful real Mooncake/HCCL transfers of 3,407,872, 3,407,872 and 19,136,512 bytes; no transport or registration mock was used. The long case exceeds Gemma's 512-token sliding window.
- Runtime provenance: the verified vLLM source above and this PR's Ascend Python source were installed in an isolated environment over the existing `v0.26.0rc1` image (CANN 9.1 / torch-npu 2.10). Native libraries and the complete custom-operator package were reused from that image, rather than rebuilt from this PR. The missing custom-op search path was corrected, and HCCL connection/execute timeouts were set to 120/204 seconds before the successful run. This validates the functional smoke in that environment; it is not a full current-main native build, graph-mode, multi-node or performance validation.

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/test_mooncake_connector.py
```

Ready for review. Both CPU UT jobs, pre-commit and DCO have passed; the CI gate awaits a maintainer-selected test label for additional precision/full tests. No serving performance claim.

items.title: [BugFix] Honor device IDs in KV transfer and native tiering offload
items.body: ### What this PR does / why we need it? With `--device-ids 1,3` and two workers, the main workers select NPU devices 1 and 3, but the Mooncake layerwise sender, SFA Remote D2H sender, and Yuanrong backend still bind their background threads directly to local ranks 0 and 1. Resolve each local rank through `current_platform.logical_device_id_to_visible_device_id()`, as the NPU worker already does, so device selection also composes with `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES`. Native tiering offload also derives its mmap partition from `current_device() % world_size`. Devices 1 and 3 both select partition 1 for world size 2, allowing one worker's KV data to overwrite another's. Use `config.parallel.rank`, matching upstream's tiering layout. Replicated layouts continue to use partition 0. This completes four Ascend-side paths affected by the device-selection changes in vllm-project/vllm#45026. It does not change CLI parsing, collective communication, or external backend SDKs. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Explicit device selection is respected by these background threads, and non-replicated native tiering workers retain separate CPU cache partitions with non-contiguous or reordered devices. Existing environment-variable selection continues through the upstream mapping helper. Release note: `release_notes/fragments/19826.yaml`. ### How was this patch tested? **Unit tests:** 214 passed, 1 existing skipped test. The three related KV/offload files passed 187 tests after the sender-initialization failure fix; the unchanged Yuanrong suite passed 27 tests in a separate process because it installs dependency mocks. Five new initialization-error cases fail against the preceding PR commit and pass after the fix. ```bash TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 python -m pytest -q \ tests/ut/kv_offload/test_npu_offload_spec.py \ tests/ut/kv_offload/test_mooncake_layerwise_connector.py \ tests/ut/kv_offload/test_sfa_pd_rd2h_connector.py # 187 passed, 1 skipped TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 python -m pytest -q \ tests/ut/distributed/test_yuanrong_backend.py # 27 passed (separate process) ``` The added tests cover non-contiguous/reordered selection, a worker rank distinct from its device ordinal, unchanged replicated layout, and sender initialization failure propagation. Earlier base-main comparison reproduced 13 focused failures while eight control cases passed. **Local checks:** Ruff check/format (0.14.0), Python compilation, `git diff --check`, staged long-function, symbolic-meta, and logger checks passed. `bash format.sh ci` was attempted on Windows; the overall command remains incomplete because some hooks require Linux executable paths, `python3`, or ShellCheck. Full Linux CI is still required. **Additional real-NPU acceptance (2026-10-26):** This run deployed all four complete production files from commit `27dde295805c58ac955ec7ea1dac7cc936ad0102` into the isolated test image; their SHA256 values were checked against that commit, allowing only checkout line endings. This is an overlay on the image's existing sources, not a complete repository deployment. Environment: Ascend910 (`Ascend910_9362`), driver 26.0.rc1, Python 3.12.13, torch 2.10.0 / torch_npu 2.10.0.post4; image vLLM 0.31.0+empty and vllm-ascend 0.19.1rc2.dev2941+g128f35ed1. Image ID: `sha256:29cb636934ed89bcead4fae593d63cdc04d70f844fcdbe983b902d6d643996a2`. Host physical devices **9,10,11,12** appear as runtime ordinals **0,1,2,3** in this container, verified after real allocation. Consequently CLI `--device-ids 1,3` selects host devices **10,12**. Other users' workloads were not modified. | Path | Observed result and acceptance boundary | | --- | --- | | Native tiering offload | **Real Qwen3-0.6B serving passed.** TP=2, mp, eager, 32 MiB device KV cache, 128 MiB CPU cache, filesystem secondary tier enabled. Three runs (offload CLI `1,3`, no-offload reference `1,3`, offload control `0,1`) completed **45 requests**, all processes exited 0, and all 15 output token sequences per run matched the reference. Each offload run completed **24 stores and 6 loads**, with successful return values; repeated prompts reused 256 cached tokens. Runtime devices `1,3` used distinct mmap partitions `0,1`. Filesystem writes occurred; filesystem readback was not separately observed. | | Mooncake layerwise PD | **Real Qwen3-0.6B P/D requests passed** on the latest commit: Prefill TP=2 + Decode TP=2 + official proxy. Env-only and CLI modes each completed **56 successful KV writes / 14,680,064 bytes**; output matched local decode and matched across modes. CLI sender threads selected `1,3`; env-control selected the same host devices. A separate CLI run without instrumentation also completed the request. **All modes still emit a heap-corruption error during teardown**, so clean lifecycle acceptance is not claimed. | | SFA/MemFabric data path | **Real protocol and payload integration passed** in both env-only and CLI modes: production sender, real ZMQ `MF_META / READ_READY_BATCH / READ_DONE`, MemFabric SDMA, and production shared-host-pool allocator. Two 4096-byte buffers (values 7 and 9) passed complete byte comparison; sender `local_rank=0` correctly selected runtime NPU 1 under CLI. This fixture uses a minimal Decode peer and is distinct from model PD. | | SFA full model PD | **Constructed small-model PD passed** in CLI and env-only modes. Two-layer DeepSeek sparse-attention config, dummy weights, real NPU execution, Prefill TP=2 + Decode TP=2, consumer sparse KV offload enabled, official proxy, 243-token prompt. Each mode completed **4 actual MemFabric reads / 1,971,712 bytes**, all returning 0; output matched the local Prefill reference and matched across modes. CLI sender threads used runtime devices 1 and 3. A dedicated observer that does not import Mooncake recorded the data path; no heap-corruption message was observed in these logs. This establishes the small-model integration path, **not production model accuracy, performance, cross-node RDMA, or a large-model deployment**. | | Yuanrong | Real NPU thread binding passed in the earlier source-verified probe; storage dependencies there were substituted. **Full storage acceptance remains blocked:** available PyPI SDK 0.8.1 lacks the multi-buffer APIs used by the integration. Current official source contains them, but the NPU SDK/service build failed at dependency acquisition: container downloads timed out; offline downloads passed official SHA256 checks for only 3 of 25 dependencies. Incorrect dependency archives were not used. | MemFabric Hybrid 1.2.1 required its official `mfcli kernel install --soc-version A3` step to build the bundled AccOffload library. Its initially zero-byte library was a build placeholder, not evidence of a corrupt wheel. Installation and subsequent real SDMA transfers succeeded. The Mooncake teardown failure was reproduced **without importing vLLM or executing this patch**: `from mooncake.engine import TransferEngine` followed by normal interpreter exit aborts with SIGABRT / `corrupted size vs. prev_size`; a torch/torch_npu-only control exits 0. This isolates an independent reproduction in the installed `mooncake-transfer-engine-npu==0.3.11.post1` environment but does not establish its underlying cause or fix. Earlier hardware probes also covered no CLI/env, env fallback, CLI `1,3`, reordered CLI `3,1`, and CLI+env: 30/30 thread bindings matched across the three paths. Real asynchronous native-offload comparison reproduced base code overwriting **11 → 12**, while the fix preserved **11 → 11**. These are additional targeted tests, not substitutes for the model results above. An extra unsorted env case (`ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3,1,2,0`) failed even in a bare torch/torch_npu control without vLLM; ascending env and reordered CLI worked. That runtime behavior remains outside the passing cases. Validation scripts, exact startup arguments, responses, transfer traces, source hashes, dependency failures, and raw logs are retained in the acceptance bundle. The PR remains **draft** because clean Mooncake lifecycle, compatible Yuanrong service integration, and full Linux CI remain outstanding. ### Checklist - [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: non-contiguous/reordered selection, non-local worker rank, and replicated layout. - [x] **Regression test**: new tests reproduce failures against the unchanged base. - [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: sender reports a device-mapping initialization failure. - [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: asserts selected devices and cache partition ownership. - [ ] **Performance impact**: no performance improvement is claimed and no benchmark was run. - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c0b6f74bee518aeaf5d72b200a0216e72fbb5e7c --- Need help on this PR? items.title: [Feature] feat: add multimodal model parameter name mapping to RLHF examples
items.body:
For multimodal models (e.g., Qwen2-VL, Qwen3.5, InternVL), the training model wraps the language model under a language_model submodule, while vLLM uses bare parameter names.
Add detection via vision_config and a mapped_params() generator to prefix parameter names with 'language_model.' when needed.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add multimodal model parameter name mapping to RLHF weight transfer examples. For multimodal models, the training model loaded by AutoModelForCausalLM wraps the language model
under a language_model submodule, but vLLM uses bare parameter names. Without this mapping, weight transfer fails silently. This PR adds vision_config detection and a
mapped_params() generator to fix the parameter name mismatch.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This is an example-only change that does not affect the vLLM API or runtime behavior.

### How was this patch tested?

Tested manually with Qwen3.5 on NPU hardware. The training model's named_parameters() correctly maps to vLLM parameter names after applying the language_model. prefix, and
weight transfer via HCCL and NPU IPC both succeed.
